basics.name: Olivier Leblanc
basics.summary: Belgian doctor in applied maths to computational imaging

work.name: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton University
work.summary: Teaching at Palmer Physical Laboratory (now 302 Frist Campus Center). While not a professor at Princeton, I associated with the physics professors and continued to give lectures on campus.

volunteer.summary: Lead organizer for the New York City branch of the People's Climate March, the largest climate march in history.
highlights: Awarded 'Climate Hero' award by Greenpeace for my efforts organizing the march.
Men of the year 2014 by Time magazine

travels.summary: Two weeks of collaborative research on radio-interferometric imaging with the Biomedical and Astronomical Signal Processing (BASP) group led by Yves Wiaux.
Two months of collaborative research on implicit neural representations with the Computational Imaging Group (CIG) led by U. Kamilov.
highlights: Invited talk at the CIG group meeting

travels.summary: One week of experimental measurements on an optical bench with a multicore fiber with the team of Hervé Rigneault.
Two weeks to learn the ICT industry, research and suggest technologies to shape global sustainability efforts.

awards.title: BASP23 Best Contribution Award
awards.summary: For my contributions to multicore fiber lensless imaging, Villars-sur-Ollon, Switzerland.

awards.title: IEEE R8 Student Paper Contest 2021
awards.summary: Best paper in the IEEE R8 Student Paper Contest 2021 for my experiments on walking droplets, Nis, Serbia.

awards.title: IEEE Best Master Thesis Award 2020
awards.summary: Best Master thesis in Electrical Engineering in 2020 for my experiments on walking droplets.

publications.name: Zur Elektrody/namik bewegter Körper
publications.summary: It concerned an interpretation of the Michelson–Morley experiment and the properties of light and time. Special relativity incorporates the principle that the speed of light is the same for all inertial observers regardless of the state of motion of the source.

references.name: Professor Yves Wiaux
references.reference: Thesis jury member and collaborator on radio interferometry.

projects.name: Quantum Computing
projects.summary: Quantum computing is the use of quantum-mechanical phenomena such as superposition and entanglement to perform computation. Computers that perform quantum computations are known as quantum computers.
